result.topic_en: Latin notes proving Abel's limit theorem for power series: the sum $\sum a_n r^n$ of a convergent series tends to the series' value as $r\to 1$, using the partial sums $\varepsilon$ and summation by parts.

$\cdots$

methods.what: Definition of the tail partial sums $\varepsilon_{n+k}=a_{n+1}+\dots+a_{n+k}$
Abel summation (summation by parts) rewriting the power series tail via the partial sums
Estimate of the tail: the terms of degree greater than $n$ are bounded in absolute value by $\varepsilon r^{n+1}$
Abel's limit theorem: as $r\to 1$ the power series approaches the sum of the convergent series

items.english: Hence it is clear that, as r converges toward the limit 1, the function finally differs from the value of the series by less than any given quantity.

items.english: The sum of the terms of degree not higher than n, however, is an algebraic function of r, which, as r approaches, is known to be able to come arbitrarily close to the sum a_1 + a_2 ... a_n.
